reason: The cited evidence directly supports CPF-induced melting, mixing, and quenching to form a W(Cu) solid solution, and shows improved radiation resistance. However, the claim of superiority over SPS and reduction of void formation is not directly supported by the cited passages, which compare only to untreated or pre-treated W, not to SPS.
premises: CPF treatment with ~100 µs pulse and ~35 J/cm² can melt and mix a thin Cu coating on W
High cooling rates (10⁶–10⁷ K/s) during CPF quench a W(Cu) solid solution
The resulting metastable W(Cu) solid solution reduces void formation and phase separation
CPF-treated W-Cu has improved radiation resistance under He ion irradiation
The CPF method outperforms conventional SPS in reducing defects and improving bonding
